# Resources for this section

RAG is already named in the comparison table on the [Generative AI overview](/generative/generative-index.qmd).

## Agents

- [5-Day AI Agents Intensive Course with Google](https://www.kaggle.com/learn-guide/5-day-agents){.external target='_blank'} — a self-paced Kaggle course: tools, memory, evaluation, and getting an agent into production.
- [15 AI Agent Projects to Build in 2026](https://amanxai.com/2026/09/11/15-ai-agent-projects-to-build-in-2026/){.external target='_blank'} — a short project list, from a first agent to MCP, multi-agent systems, and agentic RAG.
- [An Engineer's Guide to Harness Orchestration](https://agentfield.ai/blog/harness-as-black-box){.external target='_blank'} — Part 1 of a series on the agent harness as a unit of work: agency, embodiment, and persistence, and why orchestration changes around it.
[]{#cs329z}
- [Stanford CS 329Z: Engineering AI Agents](https://cs329z.stanford.edu/){.external target='_blank'} — a Stanford autumn 2026 course (Diyi Yang, Michael Ryan and John Yang) on building agentic systems: RAG, tool use and MCP, agent loops, memory, multi-agent design, optimisation, data, evals and LLM-as-judge, safety, and coding agents, with per-lecture slides and readings. Reader's guides to [Lecture 1](https://web.stanford.edu/class/cs329z/slides/lecture01.pdf){.external target='_blank'}: [History of agents](history-of-agents.qmd), [Agent architectures](agent-architectures.qmd), [Compound AI systems](compound-ai-systems.qmd), and [Key challenges in building agents](agent-challenges.qmd). Reader's guides to [Lecture 2](https://web.stanford.edu/class/cs329z/slides/lecture02.pdf){.external target='_blank'}: [What is a language model?](../generative/what-is-a-language-model.qmd), [Language model architecture](../generative/language-model-architecture.qmd), [Language model training](../generative/language-model-training.qmd), [Language model inference](../generative/language-model-inference.qmd), and [LLMs for agents](llms-for-agents.qmd).
